captures.q: What are the arguments in “Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson (EA-MANTLE-NOBEL-CARSON-2026 v0.4)” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE MANTLE OBJECT READ AS A CRITICAL PROCEDURE, ITS DISTINCTIONS KEPT: asked for the arguments of the Carson mantle object (v0.4), grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1670 through eight Goodreads chips and keeps its governing distinction: the prize is not in dispute, the motivation's account of the work is. It quotes 'The title means what the work bears.' and 'Play is one of its manners.', gives the motivation verbatim, separates compression (the class nouns oeuvre, classical tradition, new forms) from what 'playful' does, names non-possession and its three forms (textual damage, the structure of desire, bereavement), sets out the five operations and the sixth, reception (fr. 147), as the paper separates them, uses the Academy's biobibliography as the paper's internal control, and finds the paper's evidence statement ('Not read in this round: the works themselves.'), on which it rests its one reservation: the operations are specified, not performed. UNRESOLVED kept admissible. It names the substitution 'liquidation by modal substitution', a phrase the paper does not use (§2.3: '"Playful" substitutes the governing modality of the relation'). The archive is not named; no identifier.

atoms.evidence: Lee Sharks’s “Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson”
“Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson”
the Nobel Prize is not in dispute; the adequacy of the Swedish Academy’s explanation of the prize is.
Sharks calls the document a mantle object: a dated specification of what a title means
Sharks asks readers to start with the literary works themselves, identify what they do, and then test the committee’s description against those findings.
Sharks calls the document a mantle object: a dated specification of what a title means, understood through the work associated with it.
It does not dispute the Nobel award. The question is what the award’s motivation says about Carson’s work, not whether the Swedish Academy was entitled to recognize her.
Sharks wants readers to distinguish what Anne Carson’s writing actually does from the compact description the Academy attaches to it.
